summary: Requires the CPUC, by January 1, 2028, to establish new tariffs or update electric rules for interconnection and retail, transmission, distribution and generation service to participating customers, including a transmission-level interconnection tariff that assigns transmission upgrade costs to the data center, requires disclosure of duplicate applications, caps refunds at 75% of annual net transmission revenue, and imposes a 10-year early termination fee. Applies to data centers entering a new transmission-level interconnection agreement on or after January 1, 2027.

source.citation: SB 886, Chapter 438, Statutes of 2026 (chaptered text, LegiScan mirror)

notes: CORRECTION: status proposed -> adopted. Signed with six companion bills on Sept 21; earlier calendar item 'Sept 30 Newsom deadline' retired. No megawatt threshold in the enacted text. Drafting history: introduced/March drafts defined a large load customer at 75 MW peak demand; a later draft substituted 25 MW; the chaptered text drops both. Trade reporting citing 75 MW reflects the drafts.

text: This section shall only apply to a data center that enters into a new interconnection agreement to receive retail electric service at the transmission level on or after January 1, 2027.
